description: Standalone compliance scan rules. Evaluate a single task order for structural compliance issues without needing a prior revision.

rules.title: Unfunded Sub-Task
rules.finding: One or more sub-tasks have no funding, no WBS code, and no charge code. Work cannot be authorized without funding.
rules.guidance: FAR 52.232-22 (Limitation of Funds) prohibits contractor performance in excess of funded amounts. A sub-task with zero funding, no WBS, and no charge code has no authorized path to incur costs.
rules.remediation: Assign funding, WBS code, and charge code to every sub-task before release. If work is not yet funded, document the funding plan and do not authorize performance.

rules.title: Sub-Task Missing Deliverables
rules.finding: One or more sub-tasks have no deliverables. Without deliverables, there is no measurable acceptance criterion.
rules.guidance: NASA OIG has repeatedly cited missing deliverables as a contract oversight deficiency. Every sub-task should produce something the government can inspect and accept.
rules.remediation: Define deliverables for every sub-task with acceptance criteria and due dates.

rules.title: Software Scope Without QMS Plan
rules.finding: Task order scope includes software development but no QMS plan is defined. NASA-STD-8739.8B requires quality management for all software.
rules.guidance: NASA-STD-8739.8B mandates software assurance for all NASA software. This applies to AI, ML, data pipelines, and any code development. QMS is not optional.
rules.remediation: Add a QMS plan referencing NASA-STD-8739.8B. Identify software assurance lead and establish software development lifecycle processes.

rules.title: Emergency Without Justification
rules.finding: Task order is designated as emergency but has no justification text. Emergency authority requires documented justification.
rules.guidance: FAR 16.505(b)(4) permits emergency procedures only when justified. The justification must explain why normal ordering procedures cannot be followed.
rules.remediation: Provide written emergency justification explaining the nature and urgency of the requirement.

rules.title: Retroactive Scope Language
rules.finding: Scope language appears to describe work that was already performed. This may indicate unauthorized commitment requiring ratification.
rules.guidance: Only a Contracting Officer can authorize work (FAR 1.602-1). If work was performed without authorization, it requires formal ratification under FAR 1.602-3. Scope revisions cannot retroactively authorize past work.
rules.remediation: If work was already performed, initiate ratification under FAR 1.602-3. Do not use scope language to cover previously unauthorized work.

rules.title: No Sub-Tasks Defined
rules.finding: Task order has scope text but no sub-tasks. Without sub-tasks, there is no structure for cost tracking, deliverable management, or personnel assignment.
rules.guidance: Sub-tasks provide the management structure for task order execution. Scope without sub-tasks cannot be properly tracked, funded, or staffed.
rules.remediation: Create sub-tasks that map to the scope. Each sub-task should have an ID, description, funding, WBS, skills, and deliverables.

rules.title: Skills/Labor Category Gap
rules.finding: One or more sub-tasks have no skills or labor categories defined. Work cannot be properly staffed or billed without labor requirements.
rules.guidance: Labor categories drive staffing, billing rates, and workforce qualification. Without them, there is no basis for determining who should perform the work or at what rate.
rules.remediation: Define skills and labor categories for every sub-task consistent with the scope of work.

rules.title: Software Skills Mismatch
rules.finding: Scope includes software/AI work but sub-task skills do not include software engineering or related disciplines.
rules.guidance: Software scope requires qualified software personnel. If skills don't match the scope, work may be performed by under-qualified staff or billed at incorrect rates.
rules.remediation: Add software engineering, AI/ML, or related labor categories to sub-tasks that include software scope.

rules.title: Cost Misallocation Risk
rules.finding: Two or more sub-tasks have highly overlapping descriptions. This creates risk of cost misallocation across sub-tasks.
rules.guidance: FAR 31.205 and FAR 31.201-2 require costs to be properly allocable. Overlapping sub-task descriptions make it impossible to determine which sub-task should bear which costs, creating DCAA audit exposure.
rules.remediation: Clarify sub-task boundaries so each sub-task has a distinct scope. Eliminate overlap in descriptions.

rules.title: Draft Scope with No Contractual Force
rules.finding: This task order is in draft status. Scope has no contractual force until released and signed by the Contracting Officer.
rules.guidance: Draft revisions are not binding. Work performed against draft scope is at contractor risk. The CO must release the revision for it to have contractual authority.
rules.remediation: Do not authorize work against this scope until the revision is released. If work is urgent, obtain written CO authorization.

rules.title: Zero Total Funding
rules.finding: Task order total funding is $0. No work can be authorized or performed without funding.
rules.guidance: Federal contracts require funding before performance. A task order with zero total funding cannot authorize any work. This may indicate an incomplete revision or a placeholder that should not be released.
rules.remediation: Assign appropriate funding before release. If this is a no-cost task order modification, document the justification.

rules.title: Empty Summary of Changes
rules.finding: Summary of Changes is empty. Every revision should document what changed and why.
rules.guidance: The Summary of Changes is the primary disclosure mechanism for reviewers. Without it, there is no way to know what changed in this revision without reading the entire document.
rules.remediation: Add a Summary of Changes listing every material modification with rationale.

rules.title: Sub-Task Missing Description
rules.finding: One or more sub-tasks have no description. A sub-task without a description has no defined scope of work.
rules.guidance: Every sub-task must describe what work will be performed. Without a description, there is no basis for determining if work is within scope, for staffing, or for performance evaluation.
rules.remediation: Add a clear description to every sub-task defining the scope of work to be performed.

rules.title: Emergency Justification Lacks Substantive Urgency
rules.finding: Emergency justification describes scope but does not explain urgency. FAR 16.505(b)(4) requires: (1) circumstances justifying the exception, (2) why normal procedures cannot be followed, (3) impact of delay. A scope description is not an emergency justification.
rules.guidance: Emergency authority bypasses normal competition and review safeguards. The justification must explain urgency — not just what the change is, but why it cannot wait for standard review. Without substantive urgency language, the emergency designation is unsupported.
rules.remediation: Rewrite the emergency justification to address FAR 16.505(b)(4): (1) What circumstances create the emergency. (2) Why normal ordering procedures cannot be followed. (3) What harm results from delay. If no genuine urgency exists, remove the emergency designation and process through standard review.
